a: Dijkstra finds shortest paths from a source in graphs with non-negative weights.
Bellman-Ford handles negative edges and detects negative cycles.
Topological sort orders nodes in a DAG so edges go forward.
Kruskal uses Union-Find to build a Minimum Spanning Tree.
0/1 knapsack uses DP over capacity and items for optimal value.
Longest Increasing Subsequence can be solved with DP or patience sorting (O(n log n)).
Levenshtein edit distance counts insertions/deletions/substitutions between strings.
KMP searches substrings in linear time using a prefix table.
Tries power autocomplete by walking shared prefixes.
Backtracking explores candidates and reverts choices (sudoku, N-queens).
Bitmask DP tracks subsets as bits for combinatorial problems (n ≤ ~20).
On a sorted array, two pointers find a target sum in O(n).
